Separate optimization from the final scientific decision. Solve the three-variable convex profile using stable centered/scaled residuals or the quadratic H=A^T A, g=A^T b after removing any constant perpendicular term. For every true compatibility verdict, verify a primal witness lies in the original closed direct and physical balls and its full seven-component residual is within the unchanged B, permitting only the already justified signal-relative cancellation roundoff allowance. Optimizer constraint tolerances must not become radius inflation. Repair/projection of a witness is allowed only if both original constraints are rechecked and the residual is recomputed at that feasible witness; near-boundary uncertainty must trigger higher-precision/outward arithmetic or a typed unresolved outcome. Preserve exact e_d=0, Dmax=0, empty/tangent intersections and S=0 set cases.

For a false compatibility verdict with a nonempty feasible set, require a valid lower bound on the true minimum residual above B after numerical-error accounting. An approximate KKT point alone is insufficient. A suitable finite certificate is a convex dual/primal gap or a support-function lower bound. For normalized f(d)=0.5||r(d)||^2 and gradient g at a feasible d*, convexity gives lower bounds f(d*)+g·(d_obs-d*)-e_d||g|| and, if Dmax exists, f(d*)-g·d*-Dmax||g||; their maximum with zero is valid. A nonnegative-multiplier quadratic Lagrangian dual, evaluated by a stable small linear solve, can give a sharper bound. Derive whichever bound is implemented and conservatively account for all rounding in residual, gradient, support, solve and bound conversion. Use scaled norms/bounds to avoid underflow/overflow when comparing to B. If the lower and upper bounds straddle the decision boundary, return typed numerical unresolved rather than a scientific rejection. Existing cancellation allowance may account only for representational signal cancellation; it must not hide optimization error or a witness outside either physical ball. A scalar profile score may be labelled the optimum only when its bound/gap supports that accuracy; otherwise label an upper bound/interval or return unresolved. Do not silently overclaim a globally exact profile.
